paper: 2024年12月大学英语四级 第3套
limit: at least 120 words but no more than 180 words
prompt: Directions: Suppose the university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on how the students can contribute to a green campus. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
body: A green campus is not only a pleasant place to study but also a reflection of the values a university holds. As the largest group on campus, students have both the responsibility and the ability to help build it.

First, students can save resources in their daily lives. Turning off lights and air conditioners when leaving classrooms, taking shorter showers and printing on both sides of each sheet may seem like small actions, but together they make a big difference. In addition, students should reduce waste by bringing their own cups and lunch boxes, sorting garbage correctly and passing on used textbooks to younger students. Moreover, those who care deeply about the environment can join green clubs to plant trees, organize recycling campaigns and raise awareness through social media.

In short, building a green campus requires every student’s effort. If everyone starts with small things and sticks to good habits, the campus will become greener and more beautiful, and these habits will stay with students long after graduation.

paper: 2024年12月大学英语四级 第2套
limit: at least 120 words but no more than 180 words
prompt: Directions: Suppose the university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on how to enrich students’ knowledge of traditional Chinese culture. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
body: Traditional Chinese culture, with its long history and great variety, is a treasure that every young person should get to know. However, many college students today are more familiar with foreign movies and online games than with classical poetry or traditional festivals. It is therefore worth considering how to enrich their knowledge of their own culture.

First, universities can offer elective courses in subjects such as calligraphy, Chinese painting and classical literature, taught in engaging ways rather than through lectures alone. Second, student clubs can organize hands-on activities. For example, students can make rice dumplings together before the Dragon Boat Festival or learn traditional crafts like paper cutting. Such experiences make culture something to enjoy rather than something to memorize. Third, students themselves should take the initiative to read classic works and visit museums and historical sites in their spare time.

When knowledge is combined with personal experience, traditional culture will no longer seem distant. Instead, it will become part of students’ daily lives and a source of pride that they carry into the future.

paper: 2024年12月大学英语四级 第1套
limit: at least 120 words but no more than 180 words
prompt: Directions: Suppose the business school of your university is conducting a survey to collect students’ opinions on the express delivery service industry in China. You are to write a response about its recent development and its impact on people’s lives. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
body: I am pleased to share my views on China’s express delivery industry, which has grown remarkably in recent years and has changed the way people live.

The industry has expanded rapidly and improved greatly in quality. Delivery networks now reach not only big cities but also many small towns and villages. Packages that once took a week to arrive are often delivered within a day or two, and customers can track them on their phones. Meanwhile, automated sorting centers, smart lockers and, in some areas, delivery drones have made the service even faster.

These changes have made people’s lives far more convenient. Online shopping has become easy and affordable, so people can buy almost anything without leaving home. Farmers in remote areas can now sell fresh fruit to customers across the country and raise their incomes. The industry has also created a large number of jobs. However, the growing number of packages produces a huge amount of packaging waste, so companies and consumers should work together to promote recyclable packaging. Overall, the impact of the industry has been highly positive.

paper: 2024年6月大学英语四级 第3套
limit: at least 120 words but no more than 180 words
prompt: Directions: Suppose your university is seeking students’ opinions on whether university sports facilities should be open to the public. You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
body: As more people become health-conscious, whether university sports facilities should be open to the public has become a widely discussed question. I am in favor of opening them, provided that they are well managed.

There are two main reasons for my view. First, many residents, especially elderly people and children, lack convenient places to exercise, while university sports fields and courts are often empty during class hours and vacations. Opening these facilities puts idle resources to good use and encourages more people to stay active and healthy. Second, sharing facilities brings students and local residents together and builds a closer relationship between the university and the community.

Of course, opening the facilities may also cause problems such as overcrowding, noise and security risks. To prevent these problems, the university could require visitors to register with their ID cards, set specific opening hours and give students priority when the facilities are in high demand. With careful management, opening sports facilities to the public will benefit both the university and the local community.

paper: 2024年6月大学英语四级 第2套
limit: at least 120 words but no more than 180 words
prompt: Directions: Suppose your university is seeking students’ opinions on whether university canteens should be open to the public. You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
body: Whether university canteens should be open to the public has become a hot topic on our campus. In my opinion, canteens should mainly serve students and staff, and they should be open to the public only on a limited basis.

The main reason is that canteens are already crowded at mealtimes. Students often have only a short break between classes, and if large numbers of visitors came in, lines would become longer and seats harder to find. In addition, canteen meals are often subsidized by the university to keep prices low for students. Opening canteens fully to the public would strain these subsidies and might lead to higher prices. Food safety and campus security would also become harder to manage.

That said, canteens could welcome the public in a limited way, for example during off-peak hours or on weekends and holidays, when there are fewer students on campus. Visitors could also be charged slightly more than students. Such arrangements would allow canteens to share their services with the community without affecting students’ daily lives.

paper: 2024年6月大学英语四级 第1套
limit: at least 120 words but no more than 180 words
prompt: Directions: Suppose your university is seeking students’ opinions on whether university libraries should be open to the public. You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
body: Our university is seeking students’ opinions on whether the university library should be open to the public. I fully support opening the library to the public, as long as students’ needs come first.

Opening the library brings clear benefits. A university library usually has a more specialized collection than a local public library, including academic journals and professional databases. Allowing local residents to use these resources promotes lifelong learning and makes better use of what the library already has. Moreover, opening the library strengthens the bond between the university and the community around it.

However, the library is first and foremost a place for students to study, and seats are often in short supply, especially before exams. Therefore, the university could require visitors to register in advance, limit the number of visitors each day and keep certain areas open only to students during exam weeks. With such arrangements, the library can serve both students and the public well, and opening it will bring far more benefits than problems.
